shape_hint: Headless stud: a round bar threaded at both ends with a plain shank between. The short 'metal end' (length b1 ≈ 1.25 d) is screwed into the tapped hole; the longer nut end (length b, depending on the nominal length l) takes the nut. Nominal length l is measured without the metal end b1. x1 is the thread run-out next to the shank.

notes: Verified record on the layout chosen by the lead: 16 rows x 4 columns (M6-M42; b1, b l≤125, b 125<l≤200, x1), stored by the researcher as alt_rectangle. Range labels differ in spelling: globalfastener 'L≤125 / 125<L≤200', fasten.it 'l<=125 / l>125<=200', fasteners.eu 'l<125mm / 125>l<200mm', schrauben-lexikon 'l < 125 mm / l < 200 mm', Boltport 'b up to 125 / up to 200'. The meaning of x1 is given by the page drawings, not by text. globalfastener lists a newer edition 'DIN 939 - 2025' next to the 1995 page; it could not be opened (HTTP 403) and was not compared.

verification.checks_done: All pages re-downloaded by the verifier with curl (browser User-Agent) on 2026-11-11 into a separate directory (HTTP 200, text/html); tables re-read with the verifier's own parser (html.parser grid with rowspan/colspan), not the researcher's scripts or raw files. Pages: globalfastener detail_411, fasten.it din_939, fasteners.eu DIN/939, boltport din-939, schrauben-lexikon DIN_939, theo-schrauben DIN-939, woodstockindustrial din-939. Verified the 16 x 4 rectangle (M6-M42; b1_939, b_le125, b_125_200, x1) = 64 cells against 7 pages in 5 clusters: 4-5 clusters for M6-M16 and M24-M30, exactly 3 (globalfastener, fasten.it, fasteners.eu) for M18, M33, M36, M39, M42 (all four columns) and for b_125_200 of M20 and M22. Drawings of four pages opened to confirm what b1, b2 and x1 mark.
problems: German shop dataset is not counted for M20/M22 nut-end lengths: schrauben-lexikon prints 53 for M20 b2 (l < 200) (record 52); theo-schrauben prints M20 42/48 and M22 46/53 (rows shifted by one size).

M18 and M33-M42 have zero slack: globalfastener, fasten.it and fasteners.eu only. They are three separate transcriptions of the 1995 table (different label spellings; the two mass tables differ by their own typos), fasten.it's is licensed by DIN.
woodstockindustrial is counted for b (l ≤ 125) because the note under its table says the nut-end lengths apply to studs up to 125 mm (the researcher had not counted it); this changes no minimum.

x1 has no text legend on any page (fasteners.eu's legend lists only l, d, u, b1, b2 and its drawing labels both run-outs x1); the reading 'run-out at the nut-end thread' comes from the drawings of globalfastener, fasten.it and schrauben-lexikon.

Edition: a 'DIN 939 - 2025' entry exists on globalfastener; not readable (403), so it is unknown whether the current edition keeps these numbers. The table is the 1995 edition's as far as the pages say.
